_readme: A1 Trading Show livestream, 2026-08-25 -- a SEPARATE dated capture from
a1-top-setups-2026-08-24.json. Do not merge the two; compare them.
CELL-LEVEL DATA WAS ATTEMPTED AND DISCARDED. Both screenshots are dense
full-table captures -- the capture shape memory already flags as the one that
fails checksum roughly a third of the time (a1-top-setups-cells-captured.md).
The EURUSD row, the largest and clearest in the table, was transcribed cell by
cell and summed to 14 against a printed Score of 13. Per the checksum rule --
'never modify a cell just to make the total match' -- that row's 18 cells were
discarded rather than adjusted. No cell-level row from this capture is trusted.
WHAT SURVIVED: the Output column (Symbol / Bias / Score) is large, bold,
high-contrast text, distinct from the small numeric grid that failed. Two
independent screenshots, different hosts, agree exactly on all 13 rows they
share (EURUSD through AUDUSD), which is the corroboration that makes the
totals trustworthy even though the cells are not.
So this fixture carries totals only. `cells: {}` is deliberate, not an
oversight -- it says the checksum was attempted and failed, not that it was

_consistencyCheck: Captures D and E agree exactly on all 13 rows they share (EURUSD..AUDUSD), zero drift. That is the evidence the totals are real, independent of the discarded cell data.
_cellsReadme: Capture F is a DIFFERENT screenshot from D/E -- a proper multi-row table crop with
visible per-cell coloring, not a squished single-line video-frame strip -- and its
cells succeeded where D/E's attempt on EURUSD failed. No timestamp is visible in
this specific crop, so the date below is INFERRED, not read directly: the legible
rows' printed totals (NZ-DOLLAR=1, GB-POUND=0, EURJPY=4, CH-FRANC=3) match capture
D's totals for this date EXACTLY, which is the same cross-validation standard D/E's
own totals were trusted on.
TWO ROWS WERE ADMITTED AND LATER WITHDRAWN. GB-POUND and EURJPY passed the row-sum
checksum AND the total cross-check against capture D, and were written here as
trusted cells. They were wrong, and the reason is worth recording because it
invalidates BOTH of those checks as a sufficient test:
A SUM IS INVARIANT UNDER PERMUTATION. These crops have to be partitioned into
six header groups by eye (2|2|5|3|1|5 = 18). A partition that shifts a value
from one column to its neighbour adds to exactly the same total, so the
checksum passes and the printed-total cross-check passes with it.
`checkStructuralZeros` in lib/scoring/a1-legs.ts is the check that does catch it:
PCE, NFP, initial claims, ADP and JOLTS are US series and nothing else, so a row
with no dollar leg cannot carry a value in them and A1 prints 0. GB-POUND was
transcribed with pce -1, NFP +1 and claims -1; EURJPY with pce -1. Those are not
disagreements about the economy, they are arithmetic that cannot happen.
Both rows are therefore discarded ENTIRELY, not repaired -- a breach says the
partition is wrong somewhere, not where, so there is no honest way to move the
misplaced values back. Withdrawing them also retracts what they were used to
conclude: that GBPX's gap decomposes into nine economic mismatches, and that A1's
columns are not leg-differenced after all (the leg solve's self-contradicting
column count went 2 -> 8 when these two rows were admitted, and returns to 2
without them -- the 'structural finding' was these five misread cells).
EURGBP checksums correctly on its own (cells sum to 1) but that total conflicts
with capture D's EURGBP=3 for this date. Given this fixture already documents
same-day intraday drift of this size elsewhere (see the 2026-08-24 fixture's
AUDCAD: -6 -> -9 between captures B and C), it reads as probable intraday movement
rather than a transcription error -- but per the 'never silently pick a number'
rule it is not written into cells. GBPCAD is excluded on the same ground.
UK100 could not be confidently partitioned into 18 distinguishable cells from this
crop and was discarded rather than guessed.

cellsCapture.provenance: Top Setups page, three crops: (1) a multi-row table crop (NZ-DOLLAR, EURGBP, GB-POUND, UK100), (2) a two-row crop (GBPCAD, CH-FRANC), (3) a crop showing the column headers plus one row (EURJPY). Seven rows attempted, two admitted -- see rejected.

_cellsConfidence.NZDX: Passes all three checks -- row-sum (1), bounds, and checkStructuralZeros (all five US-only columns read 0) -- and its printed total matches capture D's independently recorded NZ-DOLLAR=1.
_cellsConfidence.CHFX: Passes all three checks -- row-sum (3), bounds, structural zeros -- and its printed total matches capture D's independently recorded CH-FRANC=3. LOWER CONFIDENCE THAN NZDX FOR A PROVENANCE REASON, not a checks reason: it came from the second crop of the same batch that produced the two withdrawn rows, and that crop is no longer available to re-inspect. Treat any conclusion resting on CHFX ALONE as needing a re-capture. In particular its rates cell of 0 does not agree with the 2026-08-24 solve's CHF = -1 (via EURCHF); those are different dates so it is not a contradiction, but it is not a confirmation either.

rejected.GBPX: WITHDRAWN after admission. Sums to its printed total of 0 and that total matches capture D's GB-POUND=0, but checkStructuralZeros finds pce -1, NFP +1 and claims -1 -- three US-only series on a row with no dollar leg. Discarded entirely, not repaired: see _cellsReadme.
rejected.EURJPY: WITHDRAWN after admission. Sums to its printed total of 4 and matches capture D's EURJPY=4, but carries pce -1 on a row with no dollar leg. Same treatment as GBPX.
rejected.EURGBP: cells sum to 1 (checksums against itself) but conflicts with capture D's printed total of 3 for this date -- not written to cells, see _cellsReadme
rejected.GBPCAD: cells sum to 3 and pass the structural check, but that total conflicts with capture D's printed GBPCAD=1 for this date -- excluded on the same ground as EURGBP
rejected.UK100: could not confidently partition into 18 distinguishable cells from this crop -- discarded, not guessed
